newsitem.title: UK: New U.K. government forced to delay budget - papers.
newsitem.headline: New U.K. government forced to delay budget - papers.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government has been forced to delay its first budget because of problems with its proposed windfall tax, Sunday newspapers said.

Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Gordon Brown had been widely expected to set out the budget on June 10, but this began to appear less likely at the end of last week when parliament went into recess until June 2 without the date being announced.

The Independent on Sunday said that the most likely dates were now either June 25 or July 2 -- towards the end of a two-month consultation period the government set itself in its manifesto for the election it won overwhelmingly on May 1.
Brown's budget will set out the controversial windfall tax on privatised utilities, which have made huge profits since they were sold off by the state in the 1980s and early 90s.
The Independent said "ferocious lobbying" against the tax had held up the process of drafting the budget.
At least one utility has threatened legal action against the government if it is subjected to the tax.

The conservative Sunday Telegraph said that it was not only the windfall tax that was holding up the budget. It said the large number of tax changes Brown planned in his budget were creating an "administrative shambles" at the treasury.
"There is no problem at all. The Treasury is getting on with working on the budget and when we are ready we will announce a date...
"June 10 was only a proposal, no date has been announced yet," he said.
